chunks: And with the foregoing chains of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Asim, from Fudhail al-Rassan, from Yahya ibn Aqeel, who reported that Ali, peace be upon him, said:

"I fear for you two things: following the desire of the soul and being deluded by long hope. As for following base desire, it keeps you away from the truth, and as for long hope, it causes you to forget the Hereafter.

The next world has set out approaching, while this world has departed turning its back. And each has its children. So be among the children of the Hereafter and do not be among the children of this world. Today there are deeds and no reckoning, but tomorrow there will be reckoning and no deeds."

key_terms.اتِّبَاعَ الْهَوَى: Following base desires (hawa) - abandoning rational and divine guidance in favor of carnal inclinations
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: The truth (al-haqq) - divine truth and righteous path
key_terms.بَنِي الْآخِرَةِ: Children of the Hereafter - those who orient their lives toward the next world
key_terms.طُولَ الْأَمَلِ: Long hope (tul al-amal) - excessive attachment to worldly life and procrastination in preparing for the afterlife

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the dangers of following desires and having long hopes?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) warns his followers about two spiritual dangers: blindly following base desires, which diverts from truth, and harboring prolonged worldly hopes, which makes one forget the afterlife. He uses the vivid metaphor of the Hereafter approaching while the worldly life retreats, urging believers to align themselves with the next world through action today, before the Day of Reckoning arrives.
